day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Use the morning to rest on the plane and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly Leonardo Express train or bus to the city center. Check in to your Boutique Stay in Vatican City, Borgo district. Once settled, take a leisurely stroll along the Tiber River and explore the charming Borgo neighborhood on foot. Admire the Castel Sant'Angelo from the outside — free to view from the bridge (Ponte Sant'Angelo) lined with Bernini's angel sculptures.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the Borgo district and discover Piazza del Risorgimento. Watch the sunset over the Vatican walls. Grab a relaxed first dinner at a local trattoria in the Borgo area.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick coffee and cornetto (~€2–3) at the airport upon landing.
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh supplì (fried rice ball) or pizza al taglio (pizza by the slice) from a local bakery near the hotel for around €3–5.
meals.dinner: Trattoria da Lucia or a similar family-run osteria in Borgo — try cacio e pepe or amatriciana pasta for €8–12. House wine by the carafe for ~€4.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Get your bearings, hydrate, and rest early to beat jet lag. Purchase a 48-hour or 72-hour public transport card (€7–12) at the metro station for upcoming days.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to St. Peter's Basilica — entry is FREE. Arrive by 8:00 AM to beat the crowds. Climb to the top of the dome for panoramic views of Rome (€6 on foot, €8 by elevator). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the basilica's stunning art including Michelangelo's Pietà.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through St. Peter's Square and explore the free Vatican Museums courtyard views from outside. Head to the nearby Piazza Navona (20-minute walk or short bus ride) — free to visit. Admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers and the baroque churches. Browse street artists and enjoy the lively atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to the Pantheon (free entry in the evening to view the exterior) and toss a coin in the Trevi Fountain nearby. Enjoy the magical atmosphere of Rome's historic center at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Grab a classic Italian breakfast at a neighborhood bar near the hotel — espresso + cornetto for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Pizza al taglio near Piazza Navona — try Forno di Campo de' Fiori for excellent budget slices at €3–5.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Campo de' Fiori area — look for fixed-price tourist menus (menù fisso) offering starter, pasta, and drink for €12–15. Try carciofi alla romana (Roman artichokes) as a starter.

day_by_day.notes: St. Peter's Basilica is free but requires modest dress (no bare shoulders or knees). Bring a scarf. Book dome climb tickets online in advance if possible to save time. The Trevi Fountain is most magical at night with fewer crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel — book tickets online in advance to avoid queues (€17 standard ticket, or look for last-minute deals). Spend 3–4 hours exploring the world's greatest art collection including the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican Museums, walk south toward Trastevere (about 25 minutes on foot across the Tiber). Explore this bohemian, medieval neighborhood with its narrow cobblestone streets, ivy-covered buildings, and vibrant local culture. Visit the Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere — free entry, stunning 12th-century mosaics.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Trastevere for the evening — the neighborhood comes alive after dark with locals and visitors alike. Browse artisan shops and enjoy the relaxed atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at the hotel or a nearby bar — €2–3.
meals.lunch: Eat before or after the Vatican Museums at a nearby sandwich shop (panino) — try Mercato Trionfale market area for fresh, cheap eats at €4–6.
meals.dinner: Trastevere is perfect for budget dining — try Da Enzo al 29 or similar neighborhood trattoria. Pasta dishes from €9–11, local wine from €4. Alternatively, grab a wood-fired pizza at a local pizzeria for €7–10.

day_by_day.notes: Wednesday mornings the Vatican Museums can still be busy — arrive right at opening (9:00 AM). The Vatican Museums ticket includes the Sistine Chapel. Photography is not allowed in the Sistine Chapel. Trastevere is very walkable and best explored without a map — just wander.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro (Line B) to the Colosseum — book tickets online in advance (€16 includes Roman Forum and Palatine Hill, valid for 2 days). Spend the morning exploring the iconic amphitheater. Arrive early (9:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Marvel at the 2,000-year-old architecture and learn about gladiatorial history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the Roman Forum and up Palatine Hill (included in your Colosseum ticket). These ancient ruins offer incredible insight into Roman civilization. The Palatine Hill also offers great views over the Forum. Afterward, walk to the nearby Circus Maximus — free to visit and great for a rest on the grass.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's working-class culinary heart. Explore the Testaccio Market (closes in afternoon but the neighborhood is lively all evening). Visit the non-Catholic Cemetery (free/donation) if still open, where Keats and Shelley are buried.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at a bar near the hotel — espresso and pastry for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a local alimentari (deli) near the hotel — bread, cheese, cured meats, and fruit for €5–7. Eat on the grass at Circus Maximus.
meals.dinner: Testaccio is Rome's food paradise — try Flavio al Velavevodetto or a similar local spot for offal-based Roman classics (coda alla vaccinara, rigatoni con la pajata) or stick to classic pasta. Budget €12–15 for a full meal with wine.

day_by_day.notes: The Colosseum is Rome's most visited site — booking online is essential to avoid 2+ hour queues. Wear comfortable shoes as the Forum and Palatine Hill involve a lot of walking on uneven terrain. Bring water as the Forum area has few shade spots. The Colosseum ticket is valid for 2 consecutive days — keep it for a potential return.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Borghese Gallery — one of Rome's finest art museums with works by Bernini, Caravaggio, and Raphael. Tickets must be booked in advance (€15, timed entry every 2 hours). Arrive for the 9:00 AM slot. Afterward, enjoy a stroll through the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens — free and perfect for a morning walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the bus to the Spanish Steps and the elegant Via Condotti area (window shopping only on a budget!). Toss a coin in the Trevi Fountain if you haven't already. Walk to the Pantheon — now free with a small booking fee (€5). Marvel at the 2,000-year-old unreinforced concrete dome, still the world's largest.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Jewish Ghetto neighborhood — one of Rome's oldest and most atmospheric districts. Visit the Portico d'Ottavia ruins (free, outdoor). The area has beautiful piazzas and a unique cultural atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a neighborhood bar near Borghese — espresso and cornetto for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Near the Pantheon, avoid the tourist traps — walk one block away for better prices. Try a suppli bar or grab a slice of pizza bianca from Forno Campo de' Fiori for €3–5.
meals.dinner: Jewish Ghetto cuisine — try carciofi alla giudia (Jewish-style fried artichokes, €6–8) and baccalà (salt cod) at a local restaurant. Budget €12–15 for dinner. Friday evenings here are especially lively.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery is strictly timed entry — do not be late or you will lose your slot. The gallery only allows 360 people per 2-hour session. Book weeks in advance during peak season. The Pantheon now requires a timed entry ticket — book online (€5) to avoid queues. Villa Borghese gardens are free and great for a picnic.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Capitoline Museums — the world's oldest public museums (founded 1471). Ticket costs €15 and includes access to extraordinary ancient Roman sculptures, the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, and a stunning rooftop terrace with views over the Roman Forum. Spend 2–3 hours here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Aventine Hill — a peaceful, leafy neighborhood with hidden gems. Visit the Knights of Malta Keyhole (free) — a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome through a keyhole in a garden gate. Walk through the beautiful Roseto Comunale rose garden (free, open May–June) and the Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) with panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Trastevere for a Saturday evening — the neighborhood is at its most vibrant on weekends with street musicians, locals socializing, and a festive atmosphere. Browse the outdoor stalls and enjoy the energy.

meals.breakfast: Saturday morning treat — visit a pasticceria for a proper Italian breakfast with a sfogliatella or maritozzo (cream-filled bun) for €3–4.
meals.lunch: Near Capitoline Hill, grab food from a nearby alimentari or try Mercato di Testaccio (open Saturday mornings) for incredible street food — supplì, pizza, porchetta sandwiches for €4–7.
meals.dinner: Trastevere Saturday night — share a large pizza from a local pizzeria (€7–9 each) and split a bottle of house wine (€8–10). Try Pizzeria Ivo a Trastevere for a classic experience.

day_by_day.notes: The Capitoline Museums are less visited than the Vatican but equally impressive — a hidden gem for art lovers. The Aventine Keyhole often has a short queue on weekends — arrive early or late afternoon. Saturday at Testaccio Market is the last chance to visit as it's closed Sundays. Book dinner in Trastevere in advance on Saturday nights as it gets very busy.

day_by_day.morning: Sunday morning in Rome is magical — visit the Porta Portese flea market in Trastevere (open Sunday mornings until 2:00 PM). One of Europe's largest and most famous flea markets, great for browsing vintage items, antiques, and souvenirs at bargain prices. Free to enter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon — revisit your favorite neighborhood or any missed sights. Consider a visit to the free Basilica di San Giovanni in Laterano (Rome's cathedral, older than St. Peter's) or the Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore — both free and stunning examples of early Christian art. Pack your bags and do any last-minute souvenir shopping at Campo de' Fiori.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Rome — treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal as a farewell to the Eternal City. Head back to the Borgo district near your hotel for a relaxed last evening. Enjoy a gelato from a quality gelateria (look for 'artigianale' signs) — €2–3 per scoop.

meals.breakfast: Sunday treat — grab a maritozzo con la panna (Rome's traditional cream bun) from a local bar for €3–4 before heading to the market.
meals.lunch: Street food at Porta Portese market or grab a porchetta sandwich (slow-roasted pork) from a market vendor for €4–5. Alternatively, find a local bar near the market for a quick panino.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner near the hotel in Borgo — try a full Roman meal: antipasto, pasta, secondi, and dessert. Look for a fixed menù degustazione at a local trattoria for €20–25. Splurge on a tiramisu or panna cotta for dessert — you've earned it!

day_by_day.notes: Porta Portese is cash-only — bring small bills and be prepared to bargain. Keep an eye on your belongings in crowded market areas. Sunday is a great day for church visits as many have special morning masses with choral music — a unique cultural experience. If departing on Day 8, confirm transport to the airport the night before. The Leonardo Express runs every 30 minutes from Termini station to Fiumicino airport.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Rome airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from airport to your Boutique Stay in Vatican City, Borgo district. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your room. The journey from Fiumicino takes approximately 45–60 minutes by taxi or Leonardo Express + metro.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely orientation stroll through the Borgo district. Walk along Via della Conciliazione toward St. Peter's Square for your first iconic view of the Basilica. Admire the exterior of St. Peter's Basilica and the sweeping Bernini colonnade at no cost — a perfect gentle introduction to Rome without overexerting after travel. Browse the charming local streets around Castel Sant'Angelo.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the nearby Prati neighborhood (a 10-minute walk from your hotel) for a relaxed first dinner. Explore the vibrant local restaurant scene on Via Cola di Rienzo. After dinner, enjoy a night walk across Ponte Sant'Angelo to see Castel Sant'Angelo beautifully illuminated — one of Rome's most magical evening sights.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick coffee and cornetto at the airport or on arrival — nothing scheduled pre-landing.
meals.lunch: Light bite near the hotel after check-in: try a local bar or café in Borgo for a panino and sparkling water (€8–12).
meals.dinner: Ristorante Il Sorpasso in Prati — a beloved mid-range Roman trattoria. Try cacio e pepe, supplì, and a glass of house Frascati wine (€25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Pre-book a taxi or arrange an airport transfer in advance. Confirm hotel check-in time to avoid waiting with luggage. June in Rome is warm (25–32°C), so carry water and wear breathable clothing.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel (pre-booked timed entry — book well in advance, ideally 2–3 months ahead). Start at 9:00 AM to beat the crowds. Spend 3–4 hours exploring the Raphael Rooms, Gallery of Maps, and culminating in Michelangelo's awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling. This is a world-class art experience steps from your hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the museums, visit St. Peter's Basilica (free entry, just a short walk through the Vatican). Climb to the top of the dome for panoramic views over Rome (€8 by stairs, €10 by elevator). Return to your hotel for a brief midday rest during the hottest part of the day.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the Tiber for the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk experience. Wander cobblestone streets sampling Roman street food — supplì, artichokes alla giudia, local wines — while soaking in the bohemian atmosphere of one of Rome's most photogenic neighborhoods.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or a nearby Borgo café — cappuccino and a fresh cornetto (€4–7).
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near the Vatican: Pizzarium Bonci on Via della Meloria in Prati — Rome's most celebrated pizza al taglio spot. Try 2–3 slices with creative toppings (€10–15).
meals.dinner: Included in the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk with multiple tastings. Supplement with a sit-down dessert at a Trastevere gelateria — try Fatamorgana for artisan flavors (€4–6).

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums tickets sell out weeks in advance — book online at museivaticani.va immediately upon planning. Dress code enforced: covered shoulders and knees required for both the Vatican Museums and St. Peter's Basilica. Bring a scarf or light layer. Arrive at the Vatican entrance 15 minutes before your timed slot.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market Culinary Tour — take the tram or a short taxi to Rome's most authentic food market. Join a guided culinary tour starting around 9:30 AM. Sample porchetta sandwiches, aged pecorino, fresh pasta, local cheeses, and seasonal produce. Learn about Roman food culture from local vendors who have supplied the neighborhood for generations.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market tour, explore the Testaccio neighborhood on foot — visit the Non-Catholic Cemetery (final resting place of Keats and Shelley, €3 donation) and the Macro Testaccio contemporary art space. Then head north to the Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Guided Tour (book afternoon slot, ~14:00). Walk through the heart of ancient Rome with an expert art historian guide who brings the ruins to life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Prati or Borgo area for a quieter evening. Browse local shops along Via Cola di Rienzo, then enjoy an aperitivo hour — a Roman ritual of pre-dinner drinks with complimentary snacks — at a neighborhood bar.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at hotel before the market tour — save your appetite for the tastings.
meals.lunch: Fully covered by the Testaccio Market Culinary Tour tastings (porchetta, cheese, seasonal bites). If still hungry, grab a suppli or fresh arancino from a market vendor (€3–5).
meals.dinner: Osteria Fernanda in Testaccio — a celebrated modern Roman restaurant. Try rigatoni alla carbonara and slow-roasted lamb with seasonal vegetables. Mid-range pricing (€30–40 per person with wine).

day_by_day.notes: The Testaccio Market is best experienced on weekday mornings when locals shop. Wear comfortable walking shoes — cobblestones are everywhere. The Palatine Hill & Forum combo ticket also includes the Colosseum (valid 2 days), so consider whether you'd like to add the Colosseum to a future day. Book the guided tour in advance through a reputable operator.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Experience — take a taxi or bus to Villa Borghese park (approximately 20 minutes from your hotel). Timed entry is mandatory and strictly enforced (2-hour slots); book at least 3–4 weeks ahead. Discover Bernini's breathtaking baroque sculptures — Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina — alongside Caravaggio's dramatic masterpieces in this intimate, world-class setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, spend time in the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens — rent a rowboat on the lake, stroll through the park, or visit the Pincian Hill terrace for sweeping views over Rome and Piazza del Popolo below. Descend the Spanish Steps (a short walk from the park) and explore the elegant shopping streets of the Tridente district.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the historic center around the Pantheon and Piazza Navona. Visit the Pantheon (timed entry required, €5) in the early evening when crowds thin. Stroll to Piazza Navona to admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers. Enjoy gelato and people-watching in one of Rome's most beautiful piazzas.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near your hotel — try Bar San Calisto in Trastevere if passing through, or a local Borgo bar (€5–8).
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese gardens — pick up fresh bread, prosciutto, local cheese, and fruit from a nearby deli or the Mercato Trionfale market near the Vatican before heading out (€12–16).
meals.dinner: Ristorante da Francesco near Piazza Navona — a beloved mid-range Roman institution. Try the thin-crust pizza or pasta amatriciana. Lively atmosphere, great value (€22–32 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery is one of Rome's most in-demand tickets — do not skip booking in advance at galleriaborghese.it. The gallery limits visitors to 360 per time slot to preserve the experience. June evenings are long and warm — the Pantheon and Navona area are magical at dusk. Bring mosquito repellent for the Villa Borghese gardens.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Jewish Ghetto and Campo de' Fiori neighborhood — a leisurely morning walk through one of Rome's oldest and most atmospheric districts. Visit the Great Synagogue of Rome and its museum (€12), then browse the lively Campo de' Fiori morning market for flowers, spices, and local produce. Cross to the nearby Largo di Torre Argentina — ancient Roman ruins where Julius Caesar was assassinated.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the metro or a short taxi to the Colosseum (your combo ticket from Day 3 covers entry). Explore the iconic amphitheater and imagine gladiatorial spectacles. The adjacent Arch of Constantine is free to view. Alternatively, if you've already used the Palatine/Forum/Colosseum combo, purchase a standalone Colosseum ticket online (€18). Rest at the hotel during peak afternoon heat.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere neighborhood independent evening — return to explore at your own pace without a tour. Discover hidden piazzas, local bars, and authentic Roman nightlife. Visit the stunning Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere (free, beautifully lit at night) before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a Borgo café — try a maritozzo (cream-filled Roman bun) for a local specialty (€5–8).
meals.lunch: Forno Campo de' Fiori — Rome's legendary bakery. Try pizza bianca, olive bread, and seasonal tarts. Inexpensive and authentic (€8–12).
meals.dinner: Da Enzo al 29 in Trastevere — a quintessential Roman trattoria with excellent cacio e pepe, coda alla vaccinara (oxtail stew), and tiramisù. Book ahead — very popular (€28–38 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Ghetto is particularly atmospheric on Friday mornings before Shabbat. Campo de' Fiori market runs until approximately 13:00. The Colosseum is extremely busy in June — pre-booked tickets with a timed entry are essential to avoid 2–3 hour queues. Consider adding an underground Colosseum tour for an extra fee if interested in archaeology.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip or deeper neighborhood exploration: Head to the charming neighborhood of Monti — Rome's hipster village near the Colosseum. Browse independent boutiques, vintage shops, and artisan studios. Visit the Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore (free), one of Rome's four major basilicas, with stunning 5th-century mosaics. Explore the nearby Esquilino market for multicultural food stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Palazzo Massimo alle Terme — one of Rome's most underrated museums, housing extraordinary ancient Roman frescoes, mosaics, and classical sculptures (€10). Located near Termini station, it's easily accessible. Spend 2 hours exploring before returning toward your hotel. Stop at the stunning Piazza del Popolo and its twin churches if energy allows.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell aperitivo evening in Prati — join locals at a neighborhood enoteca (wine bar) for a classic Roman aperitivo with Aperol Spritz or Negroni and cicchetti. Then enjoy a final special dinner in the Prati neighborhood, which has blossomed into one of Rome's best dining destinations.

meals.breakfast: Saturday morning treat: head to a Prati pasticceria for a full Italian breakfast — cornetto, cappuccino, and fresh-squeezed orange juice (€6–9).
meals.lunch: Mercato Monti (open weekends) — a beloved vintage and artisan market with food stalls. Grab street food from various vendors: arancini, bruschetta, local cheeses (€10–15).
meals.dinner: Osteria dell'Angelo in Prati — a legendary neighborhood trattoria serving traditional Roman cuisine with a fixed-price menu on weekends. Exceptional value and authenticity (€25–35 per person including wine).

day_by_day.notes: Monti market (Mercato Monti) runs Saturday and Sunday 10:00–20:00 — a great spot for unique souvenirs and local food. Palazzo Massimo is surprisingly uncrowded and deeply rewarding for art lovers. Saturday evenings in Prati are lively — book dinner reservations in advance. This is a good day to purchase any last-minute gifts or artisan goods.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome — attend Sunday Mass at St. Peter's Basilica (free, deeply moving even for non-religious visitors) or simply visit the Basilica one last time without the weekday crowds. Afterward, take a slow farewell walk through your beloved Borgo district, stopping at a favorite café for a final Roman breakfast ritual.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, visit any missed sites or revisit a favorite spot. The Castel Sant'Angelo museum (€15) is steps from your hotel and offers excellent views from its terrace — perfect for a final panoramic goodbye to Rome. Alternatively, spend the afternoon at a local café writing postcards or journaling. Begin packing and preparing for departure.
day_by_day.evening: If your flight departs late or the following day: enjoy a final quiet dinner in Prati or Borgo. If departing this evening, allow 2.5–3 hours to reach the airport from your hotel (1 hour travel + buffer for check-in and security).

meals.breakfast: Final Roman breakfast at your favorite neighborhood bar — savor every sip of that perfect cappuccino (€5–7).
meals.lunch: Il Sorpasso in Prati for a relaxed farewell lunch — try their Roman-style brunch spread with cured meats, cheeses, and seasonal vegetables (€18–25).
meals.dinner: Light farewell dinner if schedule permits: Pizzarium Bonci for outstanding pizza al taglio — a delicious, casual, affordable final meal (€12–18). Or a sit-down dinner at a Prati trattoria if departing the following day (€25–35).

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time — most boutique hotels require checkout by 11:00–12:00. Ask about luggage storage if your flight is later in the day. Sunday in Rome means reduced public transport — allow extra travel time to the airport. Leonardo Express trains run every 30 minutes from Termini to Fiumicino (€14 per person). Tip: book a taxi the night before for airport transfer to avoid Sunday morning availability issues.

Explore the iconic Castel Sant'Angelo (Mausoleum of Hadrian) at your own pace — its riverside setting and panoramic rooftop views make it an ideal, low-key first afternoon experience. Book a private after-hours or priority-access visit to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle evening walk across Ponte Sant'Angelo, admiring Bernini's angel sculptures at golden hour. Head to the elegant Prati neighborhood, a short stroll from the hotel, for a relaxed first dinner in Rome.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the plane or a light welcome snack at the hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Late lunch at Il Sorpasso (Prati) — a beloved Roman bistro with excellent charcuterie boards, seasonal pasta, and a curated natural wine list. Perfect for a casual yet high-quality first meal.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Il Matriciano (Via dei Gracchi, Prati) — a classic Roman trattoria beloved by locals and celebrities alike, serving impeccable cacio e pepe, abbacchio al forno, and tiramisu in an intimate setting.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light given the midday arrival and potential jet lag. The Borgo district is extremely walkable to Castel Sant'Angelo and Prati. Request your hotel concierge to pre-book Vatican Museums tickets for Day 2 if not already arranged.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel — Begin with an exclusive early-access private guided tour before the general public arrives (doors open at 09:00; VIP access from 08:00). Your expert art historian guide will lead you through the Gallery of Maps, the Raphael Rooms, and culminate in an awe-inspiring, relatively crowd-free Sistine Chapel experience. Michelangelo's ceiling and The Last Judgment deserve unhurried contemplation.
day_by_day.afternoon: St. Peter's Basilica & Dome Climb — Transition directly from the Museums into St. Peter's Basilica via the internal Vatican passage. Arrange a private guided tour of the Basilica's treasures including Michelangelo's Pietà and Bernini's baldachin. Climb (or take the elevator partway) to the top of the dome for sweeping panoramic views over Rome.
day_by_day.evening: Return to hotel to refresh. Evening aperitivo at your hotel bar or a rooftop bar nearby, followed by a refined dinner in the Prati neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — request a full Italian spread with cornetti, fresh fruit, prosciutto, local cheeses, and freshly brewed espresso.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Pizzarium Bonci (Via della Meloria, Prati) — Gabriele Bonci's world-renowned pizza al taglio with seasonal, gourmet toppings. A must-visit Roman institution, perfect between Vatican sights.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Settimio all'Arancio (near the Pantheon, a short taxi ride) — an intimate, candlelit Roman restaurant known for exceptional house-made pasta, fresh seafood, and an outstanding wine cellar. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Vatican Museums skip-the-line early access through a premium tour operator or directly via the Vatican's official website. Dress code enforced: covered shoulders and knees required for the Basilica. Wear comfortable shoes — the Vatican complex involves extensive walking on marble floors.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Experience — Take a private car to the Villa Borghese park for your timed-entry (mandatory) visit to the Borghese Gallery. Engage a private art historian guide to illuminate Bernini's breathtaking marble sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatic masterworks. The gallery limits visitors to two-hour sessions, ensuring an intimate, unhurried experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, enjoy a leisurely walk through the Villa Borghese gardens — Rome's most beautiful park. Rent a rowboat on the Pincio lake or simply stroll to the Pincian Hill terrace for sweeping views over Piazza del Popolo and Rome's rooftops. Descend to the Spanish Steps and explore the Tridente luxury shopping district (Via Condotti) for an afternoon of high-end retail therapy at Bulgari, Valentino, and Fendi.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo hour at the historic Caffè Greco (Via Condotti) — Rome's oldest café, frequented by Keats, Byron, and Goethe. Then a short taxi to dinner in the Campo de' Fiori area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel, followed by an espresso at a local Prati bar standing at the counter — the authentic Roman way.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch in the Villa Borghese gardens: have your hotel prepare or source a premium picnic hamper with mortadella, burrata, seasonal fruit, and prosecco — a quintessentially Roman luxury.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Roscioli Ristorante Salumeria (Via dei Giubbonari) — one of Rome's most celebrated culinary institutions, combining a world-class deli, wine bar, and restaurant. Order the carbonara, the burrata with anchovies, and explore their extraordinary 2,800-label wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets must be booked weeks in advance — entry is strictly timed and non-negotiable. The gallery is closed Mondays. A private guide must be arranged separately through a licensed tour operator. Comfortable walking shoes recommended for the park.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market Culinary Tour — Take a private car to the Testaccio neighborhood, home to Rome's most authentic and beloved food market. Join a premium guided culinary tour led by a local food expert: sample hand-sliced porchetta sandwiches, aged pecorino romano, supplì (fried rice balls), fresh pasta, artisanal olive oils, and seasonal Roman produce. Learn about the deep connection between Testaccio and Roman culinary identity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Testaccio neighborhood further — visit the Non-Catholic Cemetery (where Keats and Shelley are buried, a hauntingly beautiful spot), and the ancient Pyramid of Cestius nearby. Then head to the Aventine Hill for the famous Knights of Malta keyhole (perfectly framing St. Peter's dome) and the serene Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) with its panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to hotel to refresh. Private cooking class experience: arrange an exclusive evening cooking lesson with a renowned Roman chef — learn to make fresh tonnarelli cacio e pepe, carciofi alla giudia (Jewish artichokes), and a classic tiramisu. Many premium operators offer this in historic Roman apartments or private kitchens.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Lunch is incorporated into the Testaccio Market culinary tour — a progressive tasting experience across multiple market vendors and local eateries.
meals.dinner: Dinner from your private cooking class, enjoyed with your chef and fellow participants, paired with curated Italian wines. Alternatively, dine at Flavio al Velavevodetto (Testaccio) — a beloved trattoria carved into Monte dei Cocci, serving exceptional Roman classics in a unique archaeological setting.

day_by_day.notes: The Testaccio Market is open Tuesday through Saturday, mornings only (typically until 14:00). Book the culinary tour through a premium operator such as Eating Italy Food Tours or a private guide. The cooking class should be pre-booked at least two weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Guided Tour — Private art historian-led tour of the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill, the birthplace of Rome and the heart of the ancient empire. Your expert guide will bring the ruins vividly to life — the Temple of Saturn, the Arch of Septimius Severus, the House of Augustus, and the sweeping views over the Circus Maximus. Book a combined Colosseum priority-access ticket to include the underground and arena floor for an extraordinary perspective.
day_by_day.afternoon: Colosseum arena floor and underground access (included in premium Palatine Hill ticket). Afterward, explore the Capitoline Hill — visit the Capitoline Museums, the world's oldest public museums, housing the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, the Capitoline Wolf, and breathtaking views over the Forum below. The Capitoline Museums also hold exceptional ancient Roman sculpture collections.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo at a rooftop bar with Forum views (Terrazza Caffarelli atop the Capitoline Museums is ideal — check opening hours). Then dinner in the historic Jewish Ghetto neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Terre e Domus (Via della Madonna dei Monti, Monti neighborhood) — a refined restaurant celebrating Lazio regional cuisine and wines in an elegant setting, conveniently located between the Forum and Capitoline Hill.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nonna Betta (Via del Portico d'Ottavia, Jewish Ghetto) — Rome's finest Jewish-Roman cuisine, featuring legendary carciofi alla giudia, baccalà in guazzetto, and ricotta e visciole tart. A deeply authentic and historically resonant dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: The combined Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill ticket should be booked well in advance through the official Colosseo website or a premium tour operator. Underground and arena floor access requires a separate premium ticket. Wear sun protection as the Forum and Palatine Hill are largely exposed to the elements.

day_by_day.morning: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk (morning exploration version) — Spend the morning exploring Trastevere's charming medieval streets at leisure: visit the stunning Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere (one of Rome's oldest churches, with breathtaking 12th-century gold mosaics), browse artisan boutiques, and soak in the neighborhood's bohemian atmosphere before the afternoon crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon art deep-dive: visit the Palazzo Barberini (National Gallery of Ancient Art) — an underrated baroque palace housing Raphael's La Fornarina, Caravaggio's Judith Beheading Holofernes, and Hans Holbein's portrait of Henry VIII. Then explore the nearby Capuchin Crypt (Santa Maria della Concezione) — an extraordinary, macabre baroque artwork constructed from the bones of 3,700 Capuchin monks.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — Join a premium guided evening walking tour through Trastevere's cobblestone streets as the neighborhood comes alive at dusk. Sample supplì, pizza al taglio, artisanal gelato, local Roman street food, and pair with regional wines and craft beers at intimate neighborhood bars. The perfect immersive culinary and cultural evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel, then a morning espresso and fresh cornetto at a classic Trastevere bar upon arrival in the neighborhood.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tonnarello (Trastevere) — a beloved neighborhood trattoria with outdoor terrace seating, excellent cacio e pepe, and a convivial Roman atmosphere.
meals.dinner: The Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk serves as a progressive dinner experience. If still hungry afterward, nightcap and dessert at Grattachecca di San Giovanni (Trastevere riverside) — Rome's beloved shaved ice tradition, served fresh from the Tiber embankment.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday in Trastevere and the historic center is very lively — embrace the energy. Book the evening food walk through a premium operator (e.g., Walks of Italy, Devour Rome, or a private guide). The Palazzo Barberini is closed Tuesdays. Comfortable walking shoes essential for cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning — Rome's historic center is beautifully quiet on Sunday mornings. Take a peaceful walk to the Pantheon (free entry, opens 09:00) for a private-feeling experience of this 2,000-year-old architectural marvel. Then stroll to the nearby Piazza Navona — Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers at its most serene. Stop at Sant'Eustachio il Caffè for what many consider Rome's finest espresso.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon of curated luxury: visit the Palazzo Doria Pamphilj — a private princely palace still owned by the Doria Pamphilj family, housing one of Rome's greatest private art collections including Velázquez's portrait of Pope Innocent X and works by Caravaggio, Titian, and Raphael. The audio guide narrated by the current Prince Jonathan Doria Pamphilj adds an intimate, personal dimension. Finish with a farewell gelato at Fatamorgana or Giolitti — Rome's finest artisanal gelaterias.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Rome's finest table — a truly memorable send-off meal at one of the city's top restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast, savored slowly. Then espresso at Sant'Eustachio il Caffè (Piazza Sant'Eustachio) — a Roman pilgrimage for coffee lovers.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Osteria dell'Enoteca Corsi (Via del Gesù) — a hidden Roman gem operating since 1937, with a handwritten daily menu of market-fresh Roman classics and excellent house wine.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at La Pergola (Rome Cavalieri Hotel, Monte Mario) — Rome's only three-Michelin-star restaurant, helmed by Chef Heinz Beck. An extraordinary terrace with panoramic views over all of Rome, impeccable service, and a tasting menu that represents the absolute pinnacle of Italian fine dining. Reserve months in advance. The perfect luxury farewell to Rome.

day_by_day.notes: The Pantheon now charges an entry fee (approximately €5); book online to avoid queues. La Pergola requires formal attire and advance reservations — contact them directly or through your hotel concierge as early as possible, ideally months before travel. If departing the following morning, arrange a private chauffeur transfer to the airport through your hotel concierge.
